hook: A short Keter set on Mount Everest, built on an idea simple enough to state in one sentence. Most of the page is a terse radio log between a climbing team and base camp. Let the clipped messages set the pace; the subject is grim, but the file keeps it understated.
whyItMatters: It carries the prize-feature tag and earns attention through economy: one rule, one log, one closing figure. The all-caps transmission format conveys distance and thin air without ever describing the climbers. It is a good example of a Keter that frightens because of where it is rather than what it does.
thingsToNotice:
The log slides from routine to unease in small steps, while base camp's replies stay calm and formulaic, which makes the field messages feel lonelier. Watch the spelling degrade as the transmissions go on: the format itself shows the sender running short of air.

The epilogue offers a rational explanation and leaves you to decide how much it really explains. Then the second addendum changes the scale entirely, and its final line reframes the mountain itself.

related.note: Another file told through fragmentary messages rather than a report.
Another short Keter that leaves its human cost as bare numbers.
